extracted.intended_audience: authors and teams preparing Cochrane systematic reviews (review authors, methodologists, editors)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural guidance for planning, performing, analysing, and reporting Cochrane (healthcare) systematic reviews and meta-analyses, including risk-of-bias assessment and certainty-of-evidence appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, focused review question (PICO and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The review must state a clear research question specifying the populations, interventions (and comparators), outcomes, and study designs (PICO or similar) and the scope (e.g., date/language limits, settings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define primary and secondary outcomes, time-points, and eligibility for study designs up front; ensure question is answerable and clinically meaningful. Use PICO to guide search strategy and inclusion criteria; justify any limits placed on scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol development and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Review methods, eligibility criteria, planned analyses and decisions must be pre-specified in a protocol and registered (e.g., in Cochrane Register/PROSPERO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include objectives, inclusion/exclusion criteria, search methods, data extraction plans, risk-of-bias approach, and synthesis methods. Document and justify any protocol amendments with dates and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive, reproducible search strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Searches must be comprehensive (multiple bibliographic databases and sources of grey literature) and documented so they are reproducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop and report full search strategies (search terms, limits, date ranges) for each database; search trial registers, conference proceedings, reference lists, and contact experts/authors as appropriate. Avoid unnecessary language or publication-type restrictions; document search dates and any limits used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study selection using predefined criteria and transparent reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply eligibility criteria consistently; selection should be reproducible and selection decisions documented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use at least two independent reviewers for screening and selection where feasible; record reasons for exclusion at the full-text stage and present a PRISMA flow diagram or equivalent. Keep records of screening decisions and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardised data collection and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract data using piloted, standardised forms and procedures that minimise errors and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use two reviewers for extraction or verification; pilot extraction forms; extract study characteristics, participant details, outcomes, funding/conflicts; contact study authors to resolve missing or unclear data. Record decisions about calculation or transformation of data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias assessment appropriate to study design
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess risk of bias using validated tools appropriate for the study designs included (e.g., RoB 2 for randomized trials; ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess prespecified domains (randomization, allocation concealment, blinding, incomplete outcome data, selective reporting, other biases); perform assessments independently by two reviewers and provide supporting quotes/justifications. Use domain-level judgments to inform overall study risk and sensitivity analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of outcome measures and effect measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Select appropriate summary measures for dichotomous and continuous outcomes (e.g., risk ratio, odds ratio, mean difference, standardized mean difference) and justify choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer interpretable effect measures for the audience; convert measures when necessary and explain transformations. Predefine preferred time-points and prioritize patient-important outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions on whether and how to synthesise data (meta-analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide a priori whether studies will be combined quantitatively and use appropriate statistical models and methods for pooling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose fixed-effect or random-effects models with rationale; assess statistical heterogeneity (I2, Tau2), consider clinical and methodological heterogeneity before pooling, present forest plots, and describe model assumptions. Do not force pooling when studies are clinically incompatible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple arms and unit-of-analysis issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Address issues such as multi-arm trials, cluster-randomised trials, paired data, and repeated measures appropriately in analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust for clustering (e.g., effective sample size), combine or split arms correctly to avoid double-counting, account for within-person clustering in crossover trials, and apply appropriate analytic methods or sensitivity analyses as needed. Document choices and calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with missing data and attrition
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle missing outcome data transparently and assess impact on results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report extent and reasons for missing data; prefer analyses based on intention-to-treat where possible; consider plausible assumptions and conduct sensitivity analyses (best/worst case, imputation approaches) to explore impact of missing data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and exploration of heterogeneity
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate heterogeneity across studies both statistically and clinically and investigate possible sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use I2 and Tau2 measures, visual inspection of forest plots, and pre-specified subgroup or meta-regression analyses to explore heterogeneity. Interpret subgroup findings cautiously and avoid over-interpretation of post-hoc analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-specified subgroup and sensitivity analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Define subgroup and sensitivity analyses a priori to explore robustness and effect modifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit the number of subgroup analyses, base them on plausible hypotheses, present interaction tests, and interpret findings in context of multiple testing and power limitations. Use sensitivity analyses to test decisions about inclusion, risk-of-bias, model choice, and data handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of reporting biases and small-study effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess risk of publication bias and other reporting biases that could affect results and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use funnel plots and appropriate statistical tests when there are sufficient studies; search for unpublished studies and trial registries; consider selective outcome reporting and other dissemination biases when judging overall evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certainty (confidence) in the body of evidence using GRADE
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess certainty/quality of evidence for each important outcome using the GRADE approach (risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, publication bias, and other factors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present Summary of Findings tables with effect estimates, absolute risks, and certainty ratings. Provide explicit rationale for each GRADE domain decision and any upgrades/downgrades. Use GRADE to support conclusions and recommendations for practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent presentation and reporting (PRISMA and complete methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report methods and results transparently and completely, following reporting standards (e.g., PRISMA) and include necessary tables/figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide PRISMA flow diagram, complete search strategies, study characteristics tables, risk-of-bias tables, forest plots, summary tables, and plain language summaries. Make data extraction forms, analytic code, and datasets available where possible to support reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of findings in context
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret results in the context of the certainty of the evidence, balance of benefits and harms, applicability to populations/settings, and relevance to decision-makers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overstating conclusions; discuss limitations of the evidence and review methods, clinical relevance, and implications for practice and research. Use GRADE judgments to frame certainty when making recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of harms and adverse effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Include and analyse data on harms/adverse events systematically alongside benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define harms outcomes a priori, search for safety data across sources, present absolute and relative measures where possible, and discuss limitations in harms reporting and its impact on conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and appraisal of non-randomised evidence when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify when non-randomised studies will be included and apply appropriate risk-of-bias tools and synthesis methods for such evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ROBINS-I or other suitable tools, be explicit about why non-randomised evidence is needed, and handle confounding and selection bias considerations. Consider separate analyses or cautious integration with RCT evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical considerations for multiplicity and correlated outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise and address multiple outcome comparisons and correlated estimates to avoid misleading inference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify primary outcomes, interpret multiple testing with caution, consider multivariate synthesis methods if outcomes are correlated, and report how multiplicity was handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management of conflicts of interest and funding transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare financial and non-financial conflicts for review authors and record study funding to allow assessment of potential bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report authors’ conflicts and funding sources for included studies; consider sensitivity analyses excluding studies with high risk of bias due to funding or conflicts. Follow Cochrane’s policies on conflicts and editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance, peer review and editorial checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply methodological and editorial peer review to ensure standards are met before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage experienced methodologists and content experts for review; document peer-review changes; adhere to Cochrane editorial processes and methodological standards; correct errors and respond to post-publication queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating and currency of reviews (living reviews where appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for updating the review to keep it current and specify criteria/timeline for updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State search update frequency; consider living review methods for rapidly changing fields; document when searches were last run and triggers for re-running searches or updating conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and legal considerations in data use and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure ethical handling of data, respect for participant confidentiality where individual participant data are used, and compliance with copyright and data-sharing agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain necessary permissions for unpublished data, anonymise individual participant data as required, and follow data-sharing policies. Disclose any restrictions on data availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team roles, responsibilities and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Define roles (content experts, statisticians, search specialists, review managers) and ensure appropriate training and expertise within the review team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document who did what (screening, extraction, analysis); involve information specialists for searches and statisticians for complex analyses; provide training on tools (RoB, GRADE).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and reporting of advanced methods (network meta-analysis, individual participant data)
rubrics_metrics.description: When using advanced synthesis methods (network meta-analysis, IPD meta-analysis), apply and report specialized methods and assumptions transparently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify methods and assumptions, assess transitivity and consistency in NMA, describe modelling approaches, and report additional diagnostics and sensitivity analyses appropriate to the method.
